query: What signals suggest an agent's tickets will take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: resolution_days
per_column.rationale: The core target for this query -- how long a ticket took to resolve. Directly derivable from opened_at/closed_at, and evidence rows show plausible positive values. However many values are negative fractions (e.g. -0.178), which are impossible for a resolution duration and indicate a normalized/corrupted computation not supported by the timestamps, lowering groundedness.

per_column.name: priority_level
per_column.rationale: A useful axis for explaining resolution time, but it is essentially a restatement of the existing original 'priority' column, so it adds little new leverage. Values are well-grounded.

per_column.name: is_network_category
per_column.rationale: A network-vs-other flag gives a real grouping axis for resolution time. Evidence rows (VPN, intranet, internet flagged 1; database, software flagged 0) are consistent readings of category/description, though it partly overlaps the original category column.

per_column.name: same_agent
per_column.rationale: Whether assignee equals closer/opener is a plausible signal for longer resolution and derivable from original agent fields. Values look consistent with source.

per_column.name: agent_changed
per_column.rationale: Exact logical inverse of same_agent (401/99 vs 99/401), so it is a pure restatement adding no independent analytical leverage. Grounding is fine.

per_column.name: is_open
per_column.rationale: Open/closed status is relevant since open tickets have undefined resolution time (aligns with the 22 NULL resolution_days). Derivable from state/closed_at.

per_column.name: days_in_system
per_column.rationale: Values are essentially identical to resolution_days (same numbers including the impossible negatives), making it a redundant restatement. Shares the same corrupted negative values.

per_column.name: is_critical_domain
per_column.rationale: Intended as a criticality flag, but its basis is unclear: 'database' flagged critical while VPN/intranet not, with no explicit criticality signal in the source. The mapping appears somewhat asserted rather than clearly warranted, and it overlaps priority.

per_column.name: self_assigned
per_column.rationale: Constant (0 for all 500 rows). A near-constant column provides no analytical leverage. Values are not contradicted but carry no information.

judge.rationale: Several columns give genuine grouping axes for the resolution-time query (resolution_days, is_network_category, same_agent, is_open), but the set is diluted by redundancy: days_in_system duplicates resolution_days, agent_changed inverts same_agent, priority_level restates priority, and self_assigned is constant. Groundedness is generally acceptable, but resolution_days and its duplicate contain impossible negative durations indicating a corrupted computation, and is_critical_domain rests on an unclear mapping, pulling the table-level grounding down.
